questions_schema.name: urgency
questions_schema.instructions: How urgently does this ticket need a response? Levels, lowest first: none = no time element at all (general questions, curiosity, 'sometime'); some = mild time preference ('soon') or a live inconvenience worked around without loss; high = explicit deadline, money stuck or blocked now, a core action impossible today, or 'as soon as possible' said plainly; drop-everything = active loss in progress (fraud, double charge happening, card compromised), security exposure, or explicit now-markers. Urgency is not anger: a perfectly calm ticket can be drop-everything.

questions_schema.name: frustration

Levels, lowest first: calm = polite, factual or positive; concerned = worried or mildly negative wording, still civil; annoyed = clear complaints ('ridiculous', 'again', 'third time'), sarcasm, pointed criticism; angry = strong language, profanity, shouting, threats to leave, legal or regulator threats. Judge the words on the page, not the situation's objective severity.

questions.name: urgency
questions.instructions: How urgently does this ticket need a response? Levels, lowest first: none = no time element at all (general questions, curiosity, 'sometime'); some = mild time preference ('soon') or a live inconvenience worked around without loss; high = explicit deadline, money stuck or blocked now, a core action impossible today, or 'as soon as possible' said plainly; drop-everything = active loss in progress (fraud, double charge happening, card compromised), security exposure, or explicit now-markers. Urgency is not anger: a perfectly calm ticket can be drop-everything.

questions.name: frustration
questions.instructions: How frustrated is the customer's tone? Levels, lowest first: calm = polite, factual or positive; concerned = worried or mildly negative wording, still civil; annoyed = clear complaints ('ridiculous', 'again', 'third time'), sarcasm, pointed criticism; angry = strong language, profanity, shouting, threats to leave, legal or regulator threats. Judge the words on the page, not the situation's objective severity.
